BP1 activities focused on developing GFM performance metrics, conducting multi-stage EMT studies, assembling and validating detailed models, preparing commissioning frameworks, and establishing measurement and site readiness. Together, these efforts provide the analytical and engineering foundation needed for future field demonstration. 7.1 Task 1 - GFM Pre-Demonstration Studies Task 1 established the analytical, modeling, and validation foundation required to characterize the behavior of grid-forming (GFM) inverters prior to field deployment at the Wheatridge hybrid plant. Much of the work in this task centered on defining measurable performance expectations for GFM resources, understanding how those expectations manifest under realistic transmission-system conditions, and reducing technical risk ahead of commissioning in a mixed-resource environment. A major component of Task 1 was the development of a structured set of GFM performance metrics. These metrics quantify essential reliability services, angle stability support, fast frequency response, voltage-forming behavior, short-circuit current contribution, and damping performance, using attributes that can be consistently evaluated in EMT studies and small-signal analysis and, later, through Page 8 of 36 Award Number: DE-EE0010651 Recipient Name: Portland General Electric field measurements. The creation of these metrics provided the technical basis for comparing GFM behavior against grid-following (GFL) resources and for determining whether GFM controls could reliably support the bulk power system under weak-grid or disturbance conditions. Under operating conditions where the resource is not limited by power capability, energy state, or equipment constraints, the hybrid plant is expected to deliver the specified grid services, as summarized in the following table. These metrics define measurable expectations for angle support, frequency response, voltage control, current-limiting behavior, and other essential reliability functions, and serve as the technical basis for both simulation assessment and future field validation.
